newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon to deport Iraqi after questioning.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon to deport Iraqi after questioning.

text.p: Lebanese authorities decided on Monday to deport an Iraqi citizen after questioning him about the killings of several Iraqi opposition figures outside Lebanon, judicial sources said.

They said assistant military prosecutor-general Khaled Hammoud called off investigations of Bassam Yaaqoub Youssef, who had been questioned about allegedly carrying out assassinations in Kuwait, London, Morocco and Albania for Iraqi intelligence.

"It has been decided to close the case and deport Bassam Yaqoub Youssef from Lebanon after investigations proved he had not committed any crime in Lebanon and that he had legally entered the country," sources quoted Hammoud as saying.

"Even if Youssef had committed any crime, it is not within the jurisdiction of Lebanese judicial authorities to try him as long as the crime was committed outside Lebanon while no international Interpol arrest warrant has been issued against him," the judge added.
Youssef, 28, who last entered Lebanon on October 15, 1996, was arrested last Monday. On Thursday, the Iraqi embassy in Amman denied he was connected to Iraqi intelligence.
